record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: For nonlinear Schrödinger initial-boundary value problems on the half-line with Robin boundary conditions and smooth, corner-compatible initial and boundary data, can one prove that the solution is a classical solution in x>0, t>0 for a general class of nonlinearities, rather than only in special integrable cases?

evidence.quote: So the open problem here is a PDE problem, viz., to prove that the IPVP for NLS with a general class of non-linearities, with Robin boundary conditions and matching, smooth initial data, is classical in x > 0, t > 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the nonlinear Schrödinger initial-boundary value problem on the half-line:
  i u_t(x,t) + u_{xx}(x,t) + F(|u(x,t)|^2) u(x,t) = 0,  x > 0, t > 0,
with initial condition
  u(x,0) = u_0(x),  x ≥ 0,
and a Robin boundary condition
  u_x(0,t) + γ u(0,t) = g(t),  t ≥ 0,
where γ ∈ ℝ is a fixed real constant, F : [0,∞) → ℝ is a smooth nonlinearity (so that F(|u|^2) u is a general smooth nonlinear function of u, allowed to lie outside the integrable cases F(s) = ±s), and u_0 ∈ C^∞([0,∞)), g ∈ C^∞([0,∞)) are smooth and satisfy all compatibility conditions at the corner (x,t) = (0,0) needed for arbitrarily high regularity.

Prove (or disprove) that under these hypotheses there exists a solution u(x,t) which is a classical solution in the open quadrant x > 0, t > 0, i.e. u ∈ C^2 in the spatial variable and C^1 in the time variable on {x > 0, t > 0} (indeed, smooth there) and satisfies the equation pointwise, for this general class of nonlinearities F, rather than only for the special integrable cases treatable by inverse scattering / Riemann–Hilbert methods.
artifact.category_tag: Nonlinear Schrödinger IBVP on the half-line
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Fokas–Himonas–Mantzavinos, Antonopoulou–Kamvissis, Lee, Erdoğan–Tzirakis, and others) establishes local/global well-posedness in Sobolev spaces and Riemann–Hilbert representations for the half-line NLS with Robin boundary data, mostly in the integrable cubic case or for low-regularity Sobolev frameworks. A general result asserting classical (C^2 in x, C^1 in t) smoothness in x>0, t>0 for a general class of smooth nonlinearities with smooth corner-compatible Robin data does not appear to have been established in full generality; available results either restrict to integrable nonlinearities or to Sobolev (not classical pointwise) regularity. Status appears unresolved in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: The nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the half-line with a Robin boundary condition
status_evidence.snippet: Local well-posedness in Sobolev spaces H^s(0,∞), 1/2 < s ≤ 5/2, s ≠ 3/2, with Robin boundary data.
status_evidence.claim: Well-posedness results exist but in Sobolev framework, not pointwise classical regularity for general nonlinearities.

status_evidence.title: The nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the half-line with homogeneous Robin boundary conditions
status_evidence.snippet: Global weak solution and Riemann–Hilbert representation; long-time asymptotics via nonlinear steepest descent.
status_evidence.claim: Treats the integrable cubic case via RH methods, not general nonlinearities.

status_evidence.title: Regularity properties of the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the half line
status_evidence.snippet: Regularity properties studied for cubic NLS on the half-line.
status_evidence.claim: Existing regularity work focuses on the cubic (integrable) case.
